environment.qt: Qt 6.11.2; QtWebEngine 6.11.2; declared package minimum Qt 6.11.2
environment.build: Locked offline Rust workspace; public QWebEngineFrame C++ syntax check used installed Qt headers; no Rust runtime dependency or production source change.
environment.measurement_runner: Opt-in Qt Quick/WebEngine QML test at 640x480, offscreen software backend; local HTTP fixture on 127.0.0.1:8766 and cross-origin alias localhost:8766.
environment.compositor: Nested Weston startup smoke passed; wtype could not access the virtual-keyboard protocol, so native Wayland input was not sent.
environment.scope: Research-only provider prototype. No parent cross-origin DOM traversal, page bridge, private Qt API, DevTools path, or production semantic child-frame feature.

baseline_comparison: Research began from S22 evidence commit 026bebb. This commit adds only an isolated public-API probe and synthetic fixtures. Existing parent cross-origin isolation remains unchanged; no production runtime code was altered.

observations: The existing cross-origin/closed-root exterior tests passed; only the parent-visible surface was retained for cross-origin frames.
The complete gate passed 442 engine-crate tests, 144 QML/WebEngine tests, and native CTest 1/1.
Parent-world contentDocument remained inaccessible for cross-origin and opaque sandbox children, while the browser-owned ApplicationWorld provider executed against exact public frame handles.

test_results.reason: Nested Weston lacks the virtual-keyboard protocol required by wtype; editable-page native input and the T035 Wayland journey were not run.
observations: The command passed only its bounded startup smoke. Startup is not counted as cross-origin action or input qualification.

test_results.command: Inspect packaging/dependencies.toml and installed QWebEngineFrame/QWebEnginePage headers; pkg-config --modversion Qt6Core Qt6WebEngineCore; g++ -std=c++20 -Werror -fsyntax-only against Qt6WebEngineCore
observations: The package minimum is Qt 6.11.2. QWebEngineFrame C++ and QML mainFrame are documented from 6.8; QML child enumeration is documented from 6.10. The installed minimum compiled and ran successfully.
Installed public headers expose frame validity, identity equality, URL/name/size, child enumeration, and world-specific runJavaScript; no frame-created/frame-destroyed signal is present.
Cross-origin and opaque sandbox children were queried in isolated ApplicationWorld without a page bridge; only booleans and capped counts were returned.
Navigation reset the application-world document marker; removing an iframe invalidated its captured handle and fresh enumeration omitted it.
Two distinct frame handles shared URL, htmlName and size while their outer rectangles differed; the public QML frame type had no position property.

scope_amendments: Added crates/ferric-browser-engine-qt/tests/frame-probes/ as an isolated module for the S23 provider experiment; its synthetic HTML files are under the canonical tests/fixtures/webapp-interaction root. The probe remains opt-in and adds no production frame authority.
remaining_risks: The no-go is for general production cross-origin semantic targets with this public API; any narrower unique-metadata adapter would need a new exact association and geometry proof.
The installed Qt 6.11.2 minimum was compiled and exercised; unsupported older Qt versions were not built.

Frame deletion is detected through validity checks and fresh enumeration, not a public frame-destruction signal. Async completion and page teardown need explicit lifetime guards in any future integration.
The provider is browser-owned and can inspect cross-origin and opaque sandbox content; this elevated authority needs an explicit capability and consent design before production use.
Native Wayland input, live-site frames, plugin-hosted content, and nontrivial transformed frame geometry remain unqualified.
not_run_reasons: T035/native-wayland: nested Weston lacks the virtual-keyboard protocol needed by wtype; only the startup smoke passed.
No Qt version below the package minimum 6.11.2 is a declared supported target, so older builds were not tested.
